newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKS' CONE LEAVES GAME WITH SHOULDER TIGHTNESS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKS' CONE LEAVES GAME WITH SHOULDER TIGHTNESS.

text.p: New York Yankees ace David Cone, who made a successful recovery last year after surgery for an aneurysm in his pitching arm, pitched just one inning Sunday before leaving with tightness in his right shoulder.

Cone, 34, was taken to Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center and examined by team doctor Stuart Hershon. The injury was diagnosed as muscle tightness in the right shoulder. He will be re-examined on Monday.

"It could be a little bit of a tired arm and a little bit of tendinitis settling in," said Cone. "The best-case scenario is it's treatable and I could get a cortisone shot or an anti-inflammatory treatment and be back soon."

He said the doctor told him the problem did not appear related to last year's aneurysm. The right-hander did not make the trip to Anaheim with the Yankees, who open a four-game series there Tuesday night.

Cone was warming up just before the start of the second inning of the game against the Texas Rangers when he walked towards the plate to say a few words to the umpire. Shortly after, he headed directly for the dugout and went into the locker room.
"David did the right thing taking himself out. We'll have him re-examined tomorrow and see where we are with him," said Yankees manager Joe Torre.

"He had no problems warming up today, but when he went out there for the second inning to warm up, he just tightened up," said Torre. "It's not unusual for pitchers to have arm problems this time of the year."

Cone retired the first two batters in the first inning, but then seemed to struggle with his location as many of his pitches went high and out of the strike zone. He issued back-to-back walks to Rusty Greer and Juan Gonzalez, but then struck out Lee Stevens to cap off a 21-pitch first inning.
The Yankees went on to win 8-0 as Ramiro Mendoza (5-5) went six innings and Kenny Rogers struck out five of the six batters he faced for the shutout.

The 34-year-old Cone is having another solid season in his third year with the Yankees. Entering Sunday's game, his 2.84 earned run average and 214 strikeouts were both third best in the American League, and his 184 1/3 innings pitched ranked sixth.
Cone is 12-6 in 26 starts this season, but he had lost two of his previous three starts, having allowed 12 runs and 17 hits over 20 1/3 innings during that span.
Last season, Cone had surgery May 8. He went 4-1 with a 2.03 ERA to start the year, but examinations revealed a small aneurysm in the upper part of his right arm.

He came back on September 2 to pitch seven no-hit innings, and combined with Mariano Rivera on a one-hit shutout. Cone went 3-1 with a 3.94 ERA in September, and helped the Yankees to the World Series title.
Cone, in his 12th year, has a lifetime record of 148-86 in 325 games with Kansas City, the New York Mets, Toronto and the Yankees.
